course.title: TypeScript — From Beginner to Professional
course.description: A visual-first TypeScript path from JavaScript foundations and core types through advanced type programming, modules, tooling, runtime boundaries, testing, architecture, security, migration and a production-oriented capstone.
course.version_scope: Primary target: TypeScript 7.0, officially announced as available on 2026-07-08. TypeScript 6.0 is covered as a migration bridge. TypeScript 7.0 is a native Go implementation and keeps core type-checking behavior aligned with TypeScript 6.0, but deprecated TypeScript 6.0 options are rejected and ecosystem tools may require separate compatibility checks. Pin versions and confirm current official release notes before each release.
prerequisites: Basic computer literacy is sufficient to start. Basic JavaScript is strongly recommended before deeper work with functions, objects, modules, async programming and application architecture.
learning_outcomes: Explain the relationship between TypeScript source, compile-time type checking, emitted JavaScript, and runtime behavior.
Model application data with precise primitive, object, union, discriminated, generic and advanced derived types.
Configure TypeScript modules, compiler options, builds, declarations and editor/tooling workflows for a chosen runtime.
Validate untrusted input, build typed asynchronous/API boundaries, and design explicit error behavior.
Plan and test maintainable applications and libraries using architecture, security, documentation, CI and deployment practices.
